title.narrative: NMK institutionellt samarbete Miljö och EUI (SEPA)
SEPA Institutional Cooperation Environment and EU Integration

description.narrative: The objective of the cooperation project is to increase the capacity of the Ministry of the Environment and Physical Planning (MoEPP) in selected areas, to prepare for EU-accession in the environmental sector. The three areas of cooperation are i) nature protection, ii) air quality, and, iii) the screening process for EU-negotiations (Chapter 27).

Projektet "Stöd till Nordmakedoniens EU-närmande inom miljöområdet (SMEF) 2019-2021" bidrar till institutionell förstärkning av ministeriet för miljö och fysisk planering i relation till de krav som EU-integrationen processen ställer inom miljösektorn.
Projektpartnerna, Naturvårdsverket (SEPA) och Ministeriet för miljö och fysisk planering i Nordmakedonien (MoPP) har gemensamt formulerat en projektplan. Den bygger på ett tidigare långsiktigt samarbete mellan de båda myndigheterna, som ägde rum på både bilateral och regional nivå. En förstudie genomfördes under hösten 2018 för att diskutera och utveckla det föreslagna samarbetet. Fokusområden för samarbetet är: a) naturskydd; b) luftkvalitet, och c) screening-processen inför EU-förhandlingarna. Det första och tredje området innehåller även regionalt utbyte med motsvarande institutioner i grannländerna.

The project "Supporting North Macedonia in EU accession in the Environmental Field (SMEF) 2019-2021" provides support for institutional strenghtening of the Ministry for Environment and Physical Planning in response to the requirements of the EU integration process in the environmental sector. The project partners, Swedish Environmental Protection Agency (SEPA) and the Ministry of Environment and Physical Planning of North Macedonia (MoEPP), have jointly formulated the proposal for support from Sida. It is based on the previous long term cooperation between the two agencies on both bilateral and regional level. A scoping study was undertaken during autumn 2018 to discuss and elaborate the proposaed cooperation. Focus areas for the cooperation are: a) Nature protection; b) Air Quality; and, c) Screening process for EU negotiations. The first and third area will also contain regional parts, promoting learning and exchange with corresponding institutions in neighbouring countries.

sector.narrative: Public sector policy and administrative management

description.narrative:
At the time of the updating of these results, the activity period of this first project phase has been completed. Presented below is a cross-section of all results achieved throughout the activity period. Due to the absence of an explicit results framework, the project has recorded mostly output-level results, with a few notable exceptions.
A second project phase started on 1 June 2024, and will be active until 31 May 2027. The second phase builds on and integrates lessons learned from the first phase, whilst continuing to support more broadly EU accession in relation to Chapter 27 of the acquis, with a stronger focus on nature protection.
During phase I, each component is assessed by Sida to have contributed to improving the capacity of the Ministry for Environment and Physical Planning (MoEPP) to perform its tasks in its respective areas, i.e. nature protection, air quality and its overall work on EU approximation.
Sida assesses that the most successful outcome from this project was related to the development of the so-called EU Environment Academy, which brought together key staff from MoEPP as well as other environment ministries in the region and provided high-quality instruction about core EU environmental directives and the upcoming requirements brought on by the EU accession process.
The EU Environment Academy has since been taken over by several successive SwEPA-implemented projects in the Western Balkans region, and has resulted in the creation of a broad alumni network that shares experiences and information regionally between environment ministries of EU membership aspirant countries. This is expected to contribute to the preservation of institutional knowledge on the accession process throughout the region and has clear potential to catalyze cross-border cooperation in the area of environment and climate.
Summary of results per component:
Nature Protection:
- Leveraging support from Swedish County Administrative Boards, strengthened MoEPP staff capacities for managing the responsibilities from the CITES convention on illegal wildlife trade, Natura 2000 processes, wetland management, and cross-border conservation efforts. - Delivered training and workshops on biodiversity management, culminating in a successful study visit to Sweden. - Laid groundwork for contaminated land remediation through a baseline study, which identified gaps in legislative frameworks and funding mechanisms.
Air Quality:
- Upgraded monitoring infrastructure in 8 stations, enhancing the countrys ability to measure pollutants such as PM2.5, nitrogen oxides, and ozone. - Introduced advanced data management systems, enabling better reporting to the European Environment Agency (EEA). - Increased public awareness through campaigns like Warm Recommendations, focusing on reducing pollution from wood burning.
EU Accession:
- Launched the EU Environment Academy, training 35 professionals on EU environmental directives, fostering regional cooperation and knowledge-sharing. - Strengthened networks among public officials across Western Balkans, facilitating improved communication on EU integration.
Cost extension and development of new project proposal:
Sida cost-extended the project with additional funds to SwEPA in order to develop a project proposal for a second phase, with a continued focus on support to EU accession in relation to Chapter 27.
The proposal ended up with two main components - one geared to general support to EU accession and one more focused on nature protection.
A long-term advisor has been seconded to the second-phase project, initially at 20% and at 100% starting from July-August 2025.
The activity period of the second phase started on 1 June 2024 and will continue until 31 May 2027.
An inception phase that is now complete has resulted in a detailed list of activities and indicators, co-created with the Ministry for Environment and Physical Planning, which is the end-beneficiary of this intervention.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
